rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha is Makkan, Madinan, or both; Nasafi prefers both: it descended at Mecca when prayer became obligatory and again at Medina when the qibla turned to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب مكية . وقيل مدنية . والأصح أنها مكية ومدنية ، نزلت بمكة حين فرضت الصلاة ، ثم نزلت بالمدينة حين حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Fatiha is called Umm al-Qur’an on the basis of the Prophet’s statement that prayer is invalid without reciting Umm al-Qur’an.
rows.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بأم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Fatiha contains the meanings found throughout the Qur’an, it is also called al-Wafiya and al-Kafiya.
rows.anchor: ولاشتمالها على المعاني التي في القرآن ، وسورة الوافية والكافية لذلك

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A divine report calls the Fatiha a treasure from the treasures of God’s Throne, explaining its name Sura of the Treasure.
rows.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب كنز من كنوز عرشي

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls the Fatiha a healing for every illness except al-sam; this grounds its names al-Shifa and al-Shafiya.
rows.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب شفاء من كل داء إلا السام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called al-Mathani because it is repeated in every prayer; it is also called the Prayer based on reports and its obligatory status, and al-Hamd and al-Asas because it grounds the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وسورة المثاني لأنها تثنى في كل صلاة ، وسورة الصلاة لما يروى ، ولأنها تكون واجبة أو فريضة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas advises a person who falls ill or complains of pain to turn to the Fatiha, calling it al-Asas.
rows.anchor: إذا اعتللت أو اشتكيت فعليك بالأساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha has seven verses by consensus.
rows.anchor: وآيها سبع بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها
rows.claim: Medinan, Basran, and Syrian reciters and jurists, including Abu Hanifa and his followers, hold that the basmala is no verse of any sura, but is written to separate suras and for blessing; they therefore do not recite it aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: قُراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها على أن التسمية ليست بآية من الفاتحة ولا من غيرها من السور ، وإنما كتبت للفصل والتبرك للابتداء بها

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة والشافعي وأصحابه
rows.claim: Meccan and Kufan reciters and al-Shafi‘i’s school count the basmala as a verse of the Fatiha and every sura, and recite it aloud; they argue the early Muslims wrote it in the Qur’an despite orders to exclude non-Qur’anic material.
rows.anchor: على أنها آية من الفاتحة ومن كل سورة وعليه الشافعي وأصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever omits the basmala has omitted 114 verses from God’s Book.
rows.anchor: من تركها فقد ترك مائة وأربع عشرة آية من كتاب الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s dialogue dividing the Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise, glorification, and exaltation belong to God; the worshipper’s request for guidance and the response to it belong to the servant, while worship and aid are shared.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the division report begins with al-hamdu lillah, Nasafi takes it as evidence that the basmala is not part of the Fatiha; he says it is not part of another sura either, by consensus.
rows.anchor: فالابتداء بقوله { الحمد للَّهِ } دليل على أن التسمية ليست من الفاتحة ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi answers that the basmala is still Qur’an, revealed to separate the suras; its Qur’anic status does not require it to belong to a sura’s verse count.
rows.anchor: التسمية آية من القرآن أنزلت للفصل بين السور عندنا ذكره فخر الإسلام في المبسوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala’s bā’ attaches to an omitted verb supplied from context, such as ‘I read’ or ‘I recite’; a traveler, slaughterer, or other actor similarly supplies the action being begun.
rows.anchor: وتعلقت الباء بمحذوف تقديره : باسم الله أقرأ أو أتلو ، لأن الذي يتلو التسمية مقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted action comes after the basmala so the invoked name is foregrounded and exclusive: monotheists distinguish their beginning from those who invoked al-Lat and al-‘Uzza.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يقصد الموحد معنى اختصاص اسم الله عز وجل بالابتداء وذا بتقديمه وتأخير الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘Read in your Lord’s name’ the verb comes first because it opens the first-revealed sura and the command to read is more important; alternatively, read is intransitive, or the following ‘in your Lord’s name’ is the object of a later ‘read.’
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم الفعل في { اقرأ باسم رَبّكَ } [ العلق : 1 ] لأنها أول سورة نزلت في قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name relates to recitation as oil relates to growth in ‘it grows with oil’: reciting with God’s name seeks blessing and teaches worshippers to honor it.
rows.anchor: واسم الله يتعلق بالقراءة تعلق الدهن بالإنبات في قوله { تَنبُتُ بالدهن } [ المؤمنون : 20 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bā’ takes kasra because it is always a particle governing genitive, matching its vowel to its grammatical function.
rows.anchor: وبنيت الباء على الكسر لأنها تلازم الحرفية والجر فكسرت لتشابه حركتها عملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism begins with a silent consonant, so an initial hamza is added when starting speech but omitted in connected speech; some instead move the first consonant and say sim. Its ending is deleted, its original form is sumuw, and its derivation denotes elevation because naming publicizes and honors the named.
rows.anchor: فإذا نطقوا بها مبتدئين زادوا همزة تفادياً عن الابتداء بالساكن تعذراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of ism is omitted in this written basmala because it is frequent and unpronounced; the bā’ is lengthened to compensate, and ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz instructed his scribe to lengthen the bā’, distinguish the sīns, and round the mīm.
rows.anchor: وحذفت الألف في الخط هنا وأثبتت في قوله : { اقرأ باسم رَبّكَ } لأنه اجتمع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah derives from al-ilah, like al-nas from al-unas: the hamza drops and the definite article substitutes for it. Ilah once named any true or false object of worship, then chiefly the true one; Allah without hamza is exclusive to the true God.
rows.anchor: والله أصله الإله ونظيره الناس أصله الأناس ، حذفت الهمزة وعوض منها حرف التعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is a name rather than an attribute: one predicates unity and self-sufficiency of God but does not call another thing ‘a god’; divine attributes require a named subject to qualify.
rows.anchor: وأما الله بحذف الهمزة فمختص بالمعبود بالحق لم يطلق على غيره ، وهو اسم غير صفة

rows.speaker: الخليل والزجاج ومحمد بن الحسن والحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil, al-Zajjaj, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl deny that the name Allah has a derivation.
rows.anchor: ولا اشتقاق لهذا الاسم عند الخليل والزجاج ومحمد ابن الحسن والحسين بن الفضل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One derivation connects Allah with alih, ‘to be bewildered’: minds are dazed by trying to know God, which explains the spread of error and rarity of sound reflection.
rows.anchor: إذا تحير ينتظمهما معنى التحير والدهشة ، وذلك أن الأوهام تتحير في معرفة المعبود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation makes Allah a verbal noun from alaha, ‘to worship,’ meaning ma’luha, ‘the worshipped’; Nasafi compares this noun-for-participle pattern to ‘God’s creation’ meaning what He created.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو من قولهم أله يأله إلاهاً إذا عبد فهو مصدر بمعنى مألوه أي معبود

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most reciters emphasize the lām of Allah after fatḥa or ḍamma and lighten it after kasra; some lighten it in every context and others emphasize it throughout.
rows.anchor: وتفخم لامه إذا كان قبلها فتحة أو ضمة ، وترقق إذا كان قبلها كسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is fa‘lan from mercy and denotes mercy encompassing everything, like ghadban denotes being filled with anger; rahim is fa‘il. Rahman is more intensive because its form has two augmentations rather than one, and greater length signals greater meaning.
rows.anchor: والرحمن فعلان من رحم وهو الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء كغضبان من غضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A supplication calls God Rahman of this world because mercy there reaches believer and unbeliever, and Rahim of the afterlife because there it is specific to believers.
rows.anchor: يا رحمن الدنيا لأنه يعم المؤمن والكافر ورحيم الآخرة لأنه يخص المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is uniquely used as a name but broad in meaning; rahim can describe others but is specific to believers. Rahman therefore precedes the more intense form despite the usual progression from lesser to greater.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يوصف به غيره ، وعام معنى لما بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy is His beneficence toward servants, while its root sense is affection. The poet’s use of rahman for Musaylima is treated as a taunting excess in unbelief.
rows.anchor: ورحمة الله إنعامه على عباده وأصلها العطف وأما قول الشاعر في مسيلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether rahman declines depends on the proposed condition for non-declension: those requiring absence of fa‘lanah leave it indeclinable, while those requiring an existing fa‘la decline it; Nasafi prefers the first analysis.
rows.anchor: ورحمن غير منصرف عند من زعم أن الشرط انتفاء فعلانة إذ ليس له فعلانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is describing someone with praise and excellence, giving preference to the praiseworthy quality.
rows.anchor: { الحمد } الوصف بالجميل على جهة التفضيل ، وهو رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hamdu is nominative as a subject, though it can be read accusative with an implied verb as an explanatory verbal noun, like ‘thanks’ or ‘ingratitude’; nominative wording conveys a settled, enduring meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئ بإضمار فعله على أنه من المصادر المنصوبة بأفعال مضمرة في معنى الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in lillah attaches to an omitted predicate, understood as ‘due’ or ‘established.’
rows.anchor: واللام متعلق بمحذوف أي واجب أو ثابت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view treats hamd and madh as near-synonyms: both are praise and notice of beauty, whether for a blessing, courage, or noble lineage.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحمد والمدح أخوان وهو الثناء والنداء على الجميل من نعمة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike hamd, shukr is only for a blessing and can be expressed by heart, tongue, and limbs; the cited poet names hand, tongue, and the veiled heart as its three forms.
rows.anchor: وأما الشكر فعلى النعمة خاصة وهو بالقلب واللسان والجوارح قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls praise the head of gratitude and says a servant has not thanked God without praising Him; praise leads because the tongue makes gratitude more public than the hidden heart or ambiguous bodily acts.
rows.anchor: الحمد رأس الشكر ما شكر الله عبد لم يحمده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another distinction makes madh praise inherent perfections, shukr praise for beneficence, and hamd broad enough to cover both.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المدح ثناء على ما هو له من أوصاف الكمال ككونه باقيا قادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Nasafi, the definite article in al-hamd is comprehensive, against the Mu‘tazila; its attachment to Allah, the name of the divine essence, gathers all perfections and reflects the doctrine of created acts.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام فيه للاستغراق عندنا خلافاً للمعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means owner; the cited exchange has Safwan tell Abu Sufyan that being owned by a Qurayshi is preferable to being owned by a Hawazini. Rabb can also be a verbal noun used intensively as an adjective.
rows.anchor: { رَبّ العالمين } الرب المالك ومنه قول صفوان لأبي سفيان : لأن يربني رجل من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is used absolutely only of God, while for human masters it is restricted by a possessive phrase, as in Joseph’s story; al-Wasiti explains God as creator at the beginning, sustainer, and forgiver at the end.
rows.anchor: ولم يطلقوا الرب إلا في الله وحده وهو في العبيد مع التقييد

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti describes God as creator at the beginning, nourisher through provision, and forgiver at the end.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي : هو الخالق ابتداء ، والمربي غذاء ، والغافر انتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is one of God’s greatest names.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم الله الأعظم والعالم كل ما علم به الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-‘alamin may mean everything the Creator knows of bodies, substances, and accidents, or every existing thing besides God, named for being evidence of His existence.
rows.anchor: والعالم كل ما علم به الخالق من الأجسام والجواهر والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ending -in is used although normally associated with rational beings or their equivalent because ‘alamin has an adjectival sense, indicating knowledge.
rows.anchor: وإنما جمع بالواو والنون مع أنه يختص بصفات العقلاء أو ما في حكمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names al-Rahman and al-Rahim were already mentioned in the basmala; repeating them here would add no information if the basmala were part of the Fatiha, so the repetition indicates it is not.
rows.anchor: ذكرهما قد مر وهو دليل على أن التسمية ليست من الفاتحة

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh parse iyya as an independent pronoun; for Sibawayh the kaf is an uninflected address particle, while for al-Khalil it is an attached pronoun in annexation to iyya.
rows.anchor: «إيا » عند الخليل وسيبويه اسم مضمر ، والكاف حرف خطاب عند سيبويه ولا محل له من الإعراب

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans regard iyaka as a complete pronoun rather than dividing it into iyya and the kaf.
rows.anchor: وقال للكوفيون : إياك بكمالها اسم وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the object before the verb expresses exclusivity: worshippers devote worship, the utmost humility and submission, and their request for aid to God alone.
rows.anchor: والمعنى نخصك بالعبادة وهي أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل ، ونخصك بطلب المعونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shifts from speaking about God in the third person to addressing Him directly after praise establishes His attributes and greatness; the worshipper turns to the uniquely worthy addressee to worship and seek help from no other.
rows.anchor: ومما اختص به هذا الموضع أنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد والثناء ، وأجرى عليه تلك الصفات العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltifat can shift from third person to address, address to third person, or third person to first person; Nasafi illustrates the pattern with shifts in Qur’an 10:22 and 35:9 and Imru’ al-Qays’s poem, where the speaker changes person across its three lines.
rows.anchor: وهو قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن الخطاب إلى الغيبة ومن الغيبة إلى التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs favor shifts of style because they engage listeners, renew attention, and make listening more pleasurable; particular placements also carry subtleties recognized by expert scholars.
rows.anchor: والعرب يستكثرون منه ويرون الكلام إذا انتقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship precedes asking for aid either because presenting a means before asking for a need makes a response likelier, or to preserve the verse order, as with al-Rahman’s precedence despite the greater rhetorical force of the other name.
rows.anchor: وقدمت العبادة على الاستعانة لأن تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة أقرب إلى الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified request for aid embraces every kind of help; alternatively, it asks God’s help and enabling for worship, with ‘guide us’ specifying the requested assistance.
rows.anchor: ويكون قوله : «اهدنا » بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة كأنه قيل : كيف أعينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request can mean ‘keep us firm on the clear way,’ like telling someone already standing to keep standing until one returns, or ‘guide us in the future as You have guided us now.’
rows.anchor: أي ثبتنا على المنهاج الواضح كقولك للقائم : قم حتى أعود إليك أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hada is normally transitive to one object but can take another directly, as here, or with li or ila, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وهدى يتعدى بنفسه إلى مفعول واحد ، فأما تعديه إلى مفعول آخر فقد جاء متعديا إليه بنفسه كهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat means the broad road, from the verb ‘to swallow’: the road seems to swallow travelers who take it.
rows.anchor: والسراط : الجادة من سرط الشيء إذا ابتلعه كأنه يسرط السابلة إذا سلكوه

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the ṣād with a trace of zāy, since zāy is closer to ṭā’ because both are voiced.
rows.anchor: وقد تشم الصاد صوت الزاي لأن الزاي إلى الطاء أقرب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads sirat with sīn throughout the Qur’an, preserving the word’s original form.
rows.anchor: والسين قراءة ابن كثير في كل القرآن وهي الأصل في الكلمة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use a plain ṣād, the Quraysh dialect and the form preserved in the authoritative codex.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالصاد الخالصة وهي لغة قريش وهي الثابتة في المصحف الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat can be masculine or feminine, like tariq and sabil.
rows.anchor: ويذكر ويؤنث كالطريق والسبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path refers to the way of truth, the religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: والمراد به طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The path of those You favored’ is an apposition for ‘the path,’ repeating its governing element for emphasis and clarifying that the straight path is the Muslims’ path.
rows.anchor: { صِرَاطَ الذين أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ } بدل من الصراط وهو في حكم تكرير العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored people are believers and prophets, or Moses’s people before they altered their religion.
rows.anchor: وهم المؤمنون و الأنبياء عليهم السلام أو قوم موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يغيروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Other than those under anger, nor those astray’ can be an apposition to ‘those favored’ or an adjective describing them; they unite the full blessing of faith with safety from anger and error.
rows.anchor: { غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضالين } بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم ، يعني أن المنعم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ghayr normally does not become definite through annexation, it can modify the definite alladhina here: between opposites it takes definiteness, and both terms are generic yet partly specified, balancing their ambiguity and particularity.
rows.anchor: وإنما ساغ وقوعه صفة للذين وهو معرفة و «غير » لا يتعرف بالإضافة لأنه إذا وقع بين متضادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ‘upon them’ is in the accusative position as an object, while the second is in the nominative position as a subject.
rows.anchor: و«عليهم » الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية ، ومحل الثانية الرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s anger means His will to take vengeance on liars and punish them, treating them as a king does those under his authority when angry.
rows.anchor: وغضب الله إرادة الانتقام من المكذبين وإنزال العقوبة بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies those under anger as Jews, citing God’s curse and anger in 5:60, and those astray as Christians, citing their earlier error in 5:77.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى : { مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ } [ المائدة : 60 ]

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians treat la as an extra particle for emphasis.
rows.anchor: و«لا » زائدة عند البصريين للتوكيد ، وعند الكوفيين هي بمعنى غير

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians understand la here to mean ghayr, ‘other than.’
rows.anchor: وعند الكوفيين هي بمعنى غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is a spoken formula meaning ‘answer/respond,’ treated as a noun for the imperative just as ruwayd means ‘wait.’ It has long and short forms; the short vowel length is original, while the long form lengthens the hamza.
rows.anchor: آمين صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب كما أن رويد اسم لأمهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Messenger about amin’s meaning, and he answered, ‘Do it.’
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين فقال : «افعل »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem witnesses the long form amina; another line uses amin and asks God to increase the distance between the lovers.
rows.anchor: قال : يا رب لا تسلبّني حبها أبدا*** ويرحم الله عبداً قال آمينا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel taught him amin after he finished reciting the Fatiha and compared it to a seal on a letter; amin is not Qur’an because it does not appear in the codices.
rows.anchor: لقنني جبريل آمين عند فراغي من قراءة فاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura al-A‘la is Makkan and has nineteen verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وهي تسع عشرة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to declare God’s essence free of what does not befit Him; ‘the Most High’ means exalted in dominion and power, not in spatial location. Alternatively, say ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
rows.anchor: نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به ، والاسم صلة وذلك بأن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذي هو القهر والاقتدار

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed worshippers to recite it in prostration.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث لما نزلت قال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything and fashioned it evenly, not disparate or incoherent but in sound order and proportion, showing that it proceeds from a knowing, wise creator; alternatively, He fashioned each thing for its benefit and good.
rows.anchor: خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه تسوية ولم يأت به متفاوتا غير ملتئم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportioned to every animal what sustains it, then guided it to that provision and taught it how to benefit from it.
rows.anchor: قدر لكل حيوان ما يصلحه فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘guided’ implies that God also misguides, with ‘and misguides’ omitted because it is understood from parallels.
rows.anchor: أو فهدى وأضل ولكن حذف وأضل اكتفاء كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi glosses the promise as God teaching the Prophet the Qur’an until he forgets it, using that wording in his explanation of the assurance against forgetting.
rows.anchor: سنقرئك فلا تنسى } سنعلمك القرآن حتى تنساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘great fire’ is Hell, while the lesser fire is the fire of this world.
rows.anchor: يدخل نار جهنم والصغرى نار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflaha means that the person attained success.
rows.anchor: { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } نال الفوز { مَن تزكى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakka can mean cleansing oneself from idolatry, purifying oneself for prayer, or paying zakat; its form is analogous to tasaddaqa from sadaqa.
rows.anchor: { من تزكى } تطهر من الشرك أو تطهر للصلاة أو أدى الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord’s name means saying the opening takbir, and then praying the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: { وَذَكَرَ اسم رَبِّهِ } وكبر للافتتاح { فصلى } الخمس وبه يحتج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasafi uses the phrase as evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, is outside the prayer because it is conjoined to it, and may be made with any of God’s names.
rows.anchor: وبه يحتج على وجوب تكبيرة الافتتاح ، وعلى أنها ليست من الصلاة ، لأن الصلاة عطفت عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the remembrance as recalling one’s return and standing before the Lord, then praying to Him.
rows.anchor: ذكر معاده وموقفه بين يدي ربه وصلى له

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the person mentions God’s name on the way to the prayer ground and performs the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: ذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى فصلى صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura al-Fajr is Makkan and has twenty-nine verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الفجر مكية وهى تسع وعشرون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by dawn, meaning morning as in Qur’an 74:34, or by the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: { والفجر } أقسم بالفجر وهو الصبح كقوله { والصبح إِذَا أَسْفَرَ } [ المدثر : 34 ] ، أو بصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud cut into mountain rock to make houses; the passage says they were the first to carve mountains and stones and built 1,700 cities, all of stone, in Wadi al-Qura.
rows.anchor: { وَثَمُودَ الذين جَابُواْ الصخر } قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا . قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina can be accusative as a denunciation, nominative with an implied ‘they are,’ or genitive as an adjective for the previously mentioned ‘Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: { الذين } في محل النصب على الذم ، أو الرفع على «هم الذين » ، أو الجر على وصف المذكورين عاد وثمود وفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They overstepped the bounds in the lands.
rows.anchor: { طَغَوْاْ فِى البلاد } تجاوزوا الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadara ‘alayhi rizqahu means God constricted his provision and made it only enough to sustain him.
rows.anchor: أي ضيق عليه وجعله بمقدار بلغته

rows.speaker: الشامي ويزيد
rows.claim: The Syrian readers and Yazid read fa-qaddara with the strengthened consonant.
rows.anchor: { فَقَدَرَ } شامي ويزيد { فَيَقُولُ رَبّى أَهَانَنِ } أي الواجب لمن ربه بالمرصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should strive for the afterlife and not fret over immediate fortune, but reverses this: he reads abundance as honor and deprivation as humiliation, caring only for present pleasures.
rows.anchor: الواجب لمن ربه بالمرصاد أن يسعى للعاقبة ولا تهمه العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When tested by blessing and plenty, the person should be grateful; instead he claims God honored and preferred him by granting wealth, mistaking worldly abundance for honor.
rows.anchor: فإنه إذا امتحنه ربه بالنعمة والسعة ليشكر ، قال : ربي أكرمني أي فضلني بما أعطاني

words: فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When tested by poverty and restricted provision, the person should be patient; instead he calls himself humiliated because his share is small.
rows.anchor: وإذا امتحنه بالفقر فقدر عليه رزقه ليصبر ، قال : ربي أهانني فيرى الهوان في قلة الحظ من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects the claim that honor and humiliation are measured by wealth: honor comes from enabling obedience, and humiliation from being forsaken.
rows.anchor: ليس الإكرام والإهانة في كثرة المال وقلته بل الإكرام في توفيق الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each fa-yaqulu is the predicate of its subject; the first follows al-insan, with the intervening time phrase syntactically delayed, and the second predicates an implied subject. The fa follows amma’s conditional sense.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فَيَقُولُ } خبر المبتدأ الذي هو الإنسان ، ودخول الفاء لما في «أما » من معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both expanded and restricted provision are tests: abundance tests whether one gives thanks or is ungrateful, while restriction tests whether one is patient or distressed.
rows.anchor: وسمى كلا الأمرين من بسط الرزق وتقديره ابتلاء لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejects the person’s claim that wealth proves deserved honor, though He does say He bestowed and enriched him: the gift was a test, not earned; Nasafi compares the error to Qarun’s claim that his wealth came through his own knowledge.
rows.anchor: وإنما أنكر قوله { رَبّى أَكْرَمَنِ } مع أنه أثبته بقوله { فَأَكْرَمَهُ } لأنه قاله على قصد خلاف

rows.claim: Qadara ‘alayhi rizqahu means God constricted his provision and made it only enough to sustain him.
rows.anchor: أي ضيق عليه وجعله بمقدار بلغته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is a worse fault than misreading wealth as honor: although God enriches them, they fail to fulfill the duty of treating orphans kindly.
rows.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also fail to urge their own households to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: إكرام اليتيم بالمبرة وحض أهله على طعام المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is a worse fault than misreading wealth as honor: although God enriches them, they fail to fulfill the duty of treating orphans kindly.
rows.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also fail to urge their own households to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: إكرام اليتيم بالمبرة وحض أهله على طعام المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs habbahu and ahabbahu both mean ‘to love.’
rows.anchor: يقال حبه وأحبه بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamman means abundant and intense love, accompanied by greed and withholding others’ due rights.
rows.anchor: { حُبّاً جَمّاً } كثيراً شديداً مع الحرص ومنع الحقوق

rows.speaker: الحجازي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Hijazis and Abu ‘Amr have the cited reading of rabbi in the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: { رَبِّى } حجازي وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: البصري
rows.claim: The Basran reading uses third-person forms yukrimun, yahuddun, ya’kulun, and yuhibbun for the corresponding second-person forms in verses 17–20.
rows.anchor: { يكرمون } { وَلاَ يحضون } { وَيَأْكُلُونَ } { وَّيُحِبُّونَ } بصري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person means the lasting afterlife by ‘my life’ and wishes he had sent righteous deeds from this transient life ahead for that enduring life.
rows.anchor: هذه وهي حياة الآخرة أي يا ليتني قدمت الأعمال الصالحة في الحياة الفانية لحياتي الباقية
